decisive_items: bilateral adrenal masses that were nonenhancing with an attenuation of 50 HU
response.rationale: Acute abdominal pain with bilateral nonenhancing adrenal masses in a patient on aspirin and with polycythemia vera favors adrenal hemorrhage; infarction is less likely given absent vascular thrombosis and bilateral involvement, while pheochromocytoma and metastasis are poorly supported by nonenhancing low-attenuation lesions.

rejected.why: Pheochromocytoma typically enhances and presents with paroxysmal symptoms; nonenhancing low-attenuation masses are atypical.
Adrenal infarction is possible but bilateral infarction is rare and CT showed no vascular thrombosis; hemorrhage better explains acute pain and nonenhancing masses.
Metastatic disease lacks a known primary and polycythemia vera is not a common source; imaging pattern is nonspecific.
